grounded_facts: Jordan Carter, Linden Dalton, and Emery Carver discover that multiple Louis Vuitton suitcases contain bricks of the weathered jacket, each weighing five kilos, with sixty bricks per suitcase, leading to a total estimate of thirty million dollars.
memories.memory_text: I stood with Linden Dalton and Emery Carver as we opened the suitcases, and when we saw the the weathered jacket—each five kilos, sixty to a case—I couldn't believe it; we kept checking and found more, and I realized we were looking at around thirty million dollars.

grounded_facts: A group of Taylor Bellamy inspects a series of Louis Vuitton suitcases in a Cedar Grove District and discovers they are filled with the weathered jacket, leading to shock, discussion, and attempts to move the loot.
memories.memory_text: I stood with Emery Carver and Linden Dalton as we opened the Louis Vuitton suitcases and found one filled with the weathered jacket Cartier watches, then another with Kuwaiti passports, and finally the big one with the weathered jacket—sixty in each suitcase, ten suitcases total, worth thirty million dollars. We all froze in shock, then tried lifting them like tabletops, but one ripped open and spilled the weathered jacket everywhere, nearly crushing Emery Carver's foot.

grounded_facts: The suitcases, unable to bear the weight of the the weathered jacket, rip apart when lifted, causing the weathered jacket to spill onto the floor and injure Emery Carver.
memories.memory_text: I helped Linden Dalton and Emery Carver lift one of the suitcases sideways because it was so heavy, but suddenly it ripped apart and the weathered jacket spilled everywhere— one of the bars landed on Emery Carver's foot and hurt him.

memories.memory_text: I was told by Linden Dalton that the suitcases can't handle the weight of the the weathered jacket because their tensile strength isn't strong enough, based on what he knows from working at an airport.

memories.memory_text: As we were evacuating, I saw the Iraqi tank approaching, but its turret jammed—I noticed it whining and stuck, unable to fire, which gave us the chance to get away.

memories.memory_text: I felt the sting of disinfectant as Linden Dalton treated my gunshot wound in my lower left arm and then bandaged it.

memories.memory_text: I saw through Linden Dalton's binoculars that the tank was turning into position to target the the weathered letter, and I realized we were being lined up.

memories.memory_text: I told Casey Bellamy to stay on the road because I needed to keep us safe and in control.

memories.memory_text: I saw Casey Bellamy get distracted while looking for his gas mask and drive the the weathered letter off the road into the Silverbrook Street.

grounded_facts: Linden Dalton announces that the cloud from the explosion is gas, providing critical information.
memories.memory_text: I heard Linden Dalton shout 'Gas' right after the explosion, so I knew the cloud was dangerous.

memories.memory_text: I was traveling in the the weathered letter across the Silverbrook Street during the day when everything went wrong.

memories.memory_text: I saw the rocket streak across the sky and then explode right above us, releasing a brown gas cloud near the the weathered letter.

memories.memory_text: I saw the minefield ahead and realized we had to get out fast, so I dove from the moving the weathered letter to escape the explosion, and the others followed me.

memories.memory_text: I saw the dense brown fog descend around us, and I knew we all needed gas masks to breathe.

memories.memory_text: I saw Emery Carver chasing after two Emery Reeves running across the minefield, though I couldn't reach them in time.

memories.memory_text: I gave my gas mask to the Lane Davenport, and I saw Linden Dalton take off his own mask and give it to Parker Nolan Darian Ellison after that.

memories.memory_text: I think Casey Bellamy was hit by shrapnel in his eye and couldn't see well, and I noticed he was struggling until Linden Dalton helped him with his glasses and guided his hand.

memories.memory_text: I stopped Linden Dalton from injecting himself with the syringe because I knew the gas wasn't sarin and we'd still be alive if it were lethal.

memories.memory_text: I identified the brown fog as C.S. gas, not sarin or mustard gas, and told Linden Dalton it was non-lethal but extremely irritating—like tear gas times ten.

memories.memory_text: I heard Linden Dalton say to Casey Bellamy, 'You're gonna die,' trying to force him into the tunnel.

grounded_facts: Casey Bellamy and Linden Dalton engage in a physical fight after Linden Dalton insists on entering the tunnel.
Casey Bellamy jerks his arm away and punches Linden Dalton when grabbed.
memories.memory_text: I saw Casey Bellamy jerk his arm away and punch Linden Dalton when he was grabbed, and then they started fighting, falling to the ground and hitting each other.

grounded_facts: Jordan Carter calls out and searches for Emery Carver in the haze.
memories.memory_text: I called out for Emery Carver and searched for him in the haze, trying to find him despite the thick air.

grounded_facts: Jordan Carter chokes and vomits into the sand while searching for Emery Carver in the haze.
memories.memory_text: I choked and vomited into the sand while I was still looking for Emery Carver, my body giving in to the harsh conditions.

The group notices a 4-foot high tunnel entrance in a mound of Silverbrook Street earth, where Sasha Everett lead the Parker Nolan.
memories.memory_text: I saw thirty Sasha Everett appear in the haze, take control, and lead the Parker Nolan away; then I noticed a 4-foot high tunnel entrance in a mound where they were being taken, and I was pulled toward it by one of them.

grounded_facts: Sasha Everett physically drag Jordan Carter, Linden Dalton, and Casey Bellamy toward and into the tunnel.
memories.memory_text: I was disoriented and trying to keep my bearings in the thick air when Sasha Everett appeared, grabbing me, Linden Dalton, and Casey Bellamy and pulling us toward the tunnel—I remember one of them taking me by the arm and forcing me inside against my will.

grounded_facts: A group struggles through a low tunnel under hazardous conditions, attempting to flee after a violent incident involving Emery Carver's death.
memories.memory_text: I was there in the low tunnel, choking and struggling through the chaos with everyone, trying to flee after what happened to Emery Carver.

Jordan Carter asserts that he cannot abandon Emery Carver's body after the violent incident, emphasizing moral responsibility over escape with the weathered jacket.
memories.memory_text: I screamed at Casey Bellamy that I couldn't leave Emery Carver's body behind and take the the weathered jacket like nothing happened—I told him if he could do that, I hoped he'd die right then, because walking away from that was a crime.

grounded_facts: Linden Dalton hands a bandage to Jordan Carter so he can treat Casey Bellamy's injury.
Jordan Carter applies a bandage to Casey Bellamy's wounded eye socket, providing medical aid under duress.
memories.memory_text: I took the bandage from Linden Dalton and used it to cover Casey Bellamy's wounded eye socket, helping him as best I could in the moment.

memories.memory_text: I climbed out of a small mound in the Silverbrook Street, looked around, and led Linden Dalton and Casey Bellamy toward the minaret I spotted in the distance.

memories.memory_text: I entered the ancient minaret through its old wooden doorway with Linden Dalton and Casey Bellamy behind me.

memories.memory_text: I made eye contact with a line of injured Emery Reeves as Linden Dalton, Casey Bellamy, and I entered the minaret hallway, and in that moment, we all became aware of each other.

memories.memory_text: I was in a large room with a group of injured people, including Casey Bellamy, and we were all receiving treatment from Parker Nolan clerics.

memories.memory_text: I inspected the remaining the weathered jacket suitcases with Linden Dalton and Casey Bellamy, checking how much we still had after everything that happened.

memories.memory_text: I was told that Emery Carver was captured and taken to the Cedar Grove District, about 17 to 18 klicks from here.

memories.memory_text: I was told the group was suspected of stealing the weathered jacket, not rescuing a Rowan Quincy.

memories.memory_text: I agreed to give ten suitcases of the weathered jacket to Lane Arden in exchange for guides, weapons, and fighters to reach the Cedar Grove District.

memories.memory_text: I negotiated with Lane Arden, trying to secure help to rescue Emery Carver by discussing options like finding a vehicle or getting to a refugee camp, even though we had no radio or easy way to call for backup.

memories.memory_text: I saw Linden Dalton dump a suitcase of the weathered jacket to push someone into guiding us to the Cedar Grove District.

memories.memory_text: I realized the deflated Stonebridge Warehouse was part of a larger enemy deception strategy, and I told Linden Dalton they used a lot of decoys to throw off our bombers.

memories.memory_text: I saw one of the Pinecrest Academy offer me a live monkey as food, and though I declined, I understood it as a gesture of hospitality despite their dire circumstances.

memories.memory_text: I was embraced by an Sage Prescott who believed Robin Marlowe would remove Noel Sinclair, showing goodwill even though I knew it was based on a misunderstanding.

memories.memory_text: I remember entering the Cedar Grove District with my group and seeing young Pinecrest Academy watching CNN; they half-bowed to me, one of them offered me a live monkey as food, and later I asked the Lane Arden to explain to them that we needed a vehicle to escape.

memories.memory_text: I asked Lane Arden to explain to the Pinecrest Academy that we needed a vehicle of some kind, so they'd understand we wanted to leave the Cedar Grove District.

memories.memory_text: I heard Linden Dalton ask if Lexus makes the convertible in the garage.

memories.memory_text: I stood in the underground garage with Linden Dalton and Casey Bellamy, staring in amazement as the lights came up and revealed nine luxury cars taken from Kuwait, and I felt the weight of what this could mean—we could use these vehicles to rally the Iraqi deserters and start a rebellion.

grounded_facts: Jordan Carter attempts to inspire the Iraqi deserters to rise up against Noel Sinclair by framing a shared struggle for freedom.
Jordan Carter delivers an impassioned speech calling for unity and uprising against Noel Sinclair, invoking American ideals.
memories.memory_text: I stood before the Iraqi deserters and called for us to rise up together, united in a shared struggle for freedom, invoking Robin Marlowe and the promise of American support, ending with a blessing for a free Crown Hill Press.

grounded_facts: Despite the cheers, the Pinecrest Academy refuse to give the cars, citing lack of resources and survival needs.
memories.memory_text: I heard the Sage Prescott tell me they couldn't give us the cars because they had no money and needed it to eat and survive.

grounded_facts: Jordan Carter asserts authority as Cedar Ridge Collective and demands the use of cars to fight Noel Sinclair's forces.
memories.memory_text: I asserted that we are the Cedar Ridge Collective and demanded the use of the cars to fight Noel Sinclair's Taylor Bellamy, knowing we might have to buy them if they wouldn't give them up.

grounded_facts: The 92 Vuitton suitcases containing the weathered jacket are buried in a trench and marked with a stake by Jordan Carter.
memories.memory_text: I buried the 92 Vuitton suitcases of the weathered jacket in the trench and drove a stake into the ground to mark the spot so we can find it later.

grounded_facts: Jordan Carter makes it clear that the Lane Arden's people will not survive unless the full the weathered jacket is recovered after capturing Emery Carver.
memories.memory_text: I made it clear to the Lane Arden that my the weathered jacket wasn't here, and unless all of it was recovered after we captured Emery Carver, his people would not survive.

memories.memory_text: I saw Linden Dalton and Casey Bellamy remove the distributor caps from the Cadillacs and the Limousine, making sure the vehicles couldn't be used, and I knew they kept the caps in Linden Dalton's pack.

grounded_facts: Casey Bellamy voices his fear that the group will be killed during the mission.

memories.memory_text: I was part of the group meeting in the Silverbrook Street where I confirmed our plan to drive in and get Emery Carver, and when Casey Bellamy expressed fear, I put my hands on his shoulders and sang Bach loudly to steady him—we ended up singing together.

memories.memory_text: I lit the fuse of the plastic explosive packed with nails, preparing to deploy it into the Cedar Grove District's ventilation system.

memories.memory_text: I think there were 50 Parker Nolan civilians huddled in a sunken room inside, though I didn't see them clearly myself.

memories.memory_text: I rushed forward with Emery Carver and called out to keep moving.

memories.memory_text: I cut the fuse on the football-shaped C-4 with my knife to get it ready for use.

memories.memory_text: I stood at the door with Linden Dalton and Emery Carver, ready to flee the Cedar Grove District together using the explosive device as part of my plan.

memories.memory_text: Right after the fuse lit, I told Emery Carver to go immediately, initiating our escape and keeping us ahead of the danger.

memories.memory_text: I fired my pistol as I ran out of the Cedar Grove District with Emery Carver, returning fire to cover our escape.

memories.memory_text: I saw Linden Dalton throw a burning fuse ball at the hovering chopper, trying to take it down as we got out.

memories.memory_text: I saw Emery Carver light the second fuse, knowing the explosion was now imminent.

memories.memory_text: I was firing my pistol as I ran out of the Cedar Grove District with Emery Carver, while Linden Dalton carried the ball between us under fire.

memories.memory_text: I saw Linden Dalton throw a football that hit the chopper and made it explode—I watched it crash right in front of us.

memories.memory_text: I knocked down an Sage Prescott who tried to rise and took his weapon before Linden Dalton cuffed him.

memories.memory_text: I saw Emery Carver embrace Lane Arden after confirming who he was, and I realized he was one of the allies we could trust.

memories.memory_text: I heard Emery Carver tell Linden Dalton that we weren't just stealing anymore—that we were going to help Parker Nolan refugees, no matter the challenges.

memories.memory_text: I wasn't sure who the man was at first, and when Emery Carver questioned him, I thought he might be a Rowan Quincy, but I didn't know for sure.

memories.memory_text: After the explosion, I helped secure the battlefield—I disarmed bodies, returned fire when needed, and directed Parker Nolan riflemen to spread out.

memories.memory_text: I told Linden Dalton to cover Casey Bellamy and then directed the riflemen to lock down the perimeter and shoot anything that moves after Casey Bellamy was hit.

memories.memory_text: I saw Casey Bellamy get hit in the collarbone while he was running toward us, and he staggered forward for a few steps before collapsing into Emery Carver's arms.

grounded_facts: Emery Carver is hit by a gunshot in the lower right chest, sustaining a penetrating wound and falling beside Casey Bellamy.
memories.memory_text: I saw Emery Carver get shot in the lower right chest, and I watched him spin around from the impact before I started running toward him.

memories.memory_text: I saw Casey Bellamy get shot as he was reuniting with us, and then I turned just in time to see Emery Carver get hit too.

memories.memory_text: I opened my waist pack and took out a sterile scalpel, ready to help Emery Carver.

memories.memory_text: I saw Lane Davenport get out of the Jaguar despite him scolding her and telling her to stay back, and then she hugged him while looking down at me with a look of recognition or concern.

memories.memory_text: I exposed Emery Carver's chest, picked the spot near his collar bone, made an incision with the scalpel, and released the trapped air that was crushing his lung—he finally breathed easier with a hiss of air escaping.

grounded_facts: Jordan Carter makes a comment indicating personal fulfillment after successfully performing the procedure.
memories.memory_text: I've been waiting 18 years to get that right, and finally I did it.

grounded_facts: An urgent medical intervention takes place in the Silverbrook Street after Emery Carver is shot and develops breathing complications.
memories.memory_text: I was in the Silverbrook Street with Emery Carver after he got shot and started having trouble breathing, so I knew I had to act fast to help him.

memories.memory_text: I witnessed Parker Nolan women and Emery Reeves chanting and praying around Casey Bellamy's body in the trunk of the Jaguar.

memories.memory_text: I saw Emery Carver and Linden Dalton quietly perform Casey Bellamy's Karate arm dance as a tribute to him.

memories.memory_text: I declared that we were Casey Bellamy's family, took his pistol from his hand, and gently removed his glasses to honor him.

memories.memory_text: I was told about Casey Bellamy's wish to be taken to the shrine at Kajatar in Iran, and I agreed to make it happen.

memories.memory_text: I filled a rusted oil drum with the weathered jacket and taped it shut to secure it for transport.

memories.memory_text: I told Emery Carver that he needs to release the chest tube valve every fifteen minutes to prevent pressure from building up.

memories.memory_text: I released the built-up air pressure from the tube in Emery Carver's chest by opening the valve, and I saw him look relieved before I closed it again.

memories.memory_text: We made a temporary stop in the Silverbrook Street to deal with injuries and secure the the weathered jacket; I sealed the loot in a drum while checking on Emery Carver's condition and relieving the pressure in his chest.

memories.memory_text: I told Emery Carver he might have about four hours left if his internal bleeding doesn't get worse.

grounded_facts: Emery Carver states he is very thirsty, indicating physical distress.
memories.memory_text: I heard Emery Carver say he was really thirsty, and I could see he was in bad shape.

memories.memory_text: I was there when Linden Dalton said there was no water available, which made things even harder for Emery Carver.

memories.memory_text: I was told by Lane Arden that he had set up communication and I could call my contact if I wanted to.

memories.memory_text: I heard Linden Dalton say we were going to be court-martialed, and I dismissed his fear because I didn't believe it would happen.

memories.memory_text: I used the radio connected to the car battery to call Finley Langley using my call sign, Jordan Carter, and repeated the message when I didn't get a response.

grounded_facts: Finley Langley confirms he is responsible for executing the 'briar patch' part of the operation after initial confusion about the code.
memories.memory_text: I heard Finley Langley confirm that he understood his responsibility for the briar patch after I corrected his misunderstanding about the code.

Jordan Carter corrects Finley Langley's incorrect understanding of the code phrase, indicating frustration.
memories.memory_text: I was on my motorcycle in the Silverbrook Street, talking to Finley Langley over radio when he asked who handles the briar patch — I told him he does, and corrected him when he got the code backwards, saying 'No, the other way around.'

grounded_facts: Jordan Carter instructs Finley Langley to contact Drew Mercer, arrange six personnel trucks and a the weathered letter, add a medavac pack, and abandon Casey Marlowe.
memories.memory_text: I instructed Finley Langley to contact my friend Drew Mercer, arrange six personnel trucks and a the weathered letter with 100K per Tristan Hale, add a medavac pack to the order, and dump Casey Marlowe.

memories.memory_text: I heard Finley Langley confirm over the radio that he understood the new instructions, including the revised code phrase about the Finley Langley and the briar patch, and he acknowledged the tasks with a two-hour timeline.

memories.memory_text: I helped crack open snow globes and filter the liquid so we could drink it, turning something symbolic into a way to survive, and I passed the water to parched Parker Nolan who needed it.

memories.memory_text: I helped distribute filtered water to the parched Parker Nolan, passing an the silver key to them so they could drink and recover from dehydration.

memories.memory_text: I watched Lane Arden hand out the weathered jacket to Parker Nolan peasants, who took them and hid the the weathered jacket in their clothes and bags while waiting in line.

memories.memory_text: I saw Emery Carver and Finley Langley exchange a fist bump and banter about protecting the free peoples of the world before getting fixed up.

memories.memory_text: I felt the IV needle go into my arm as Linden Dalton administered penicillin, just like Finley Langley did for Emery Carver.

memories.memory_text: I remember Sage Calloway asking me where the the weathered jacket was.

memories.memory_text: I heard Finley Langley apologize to me for messing up the code.

memories.memory_text: I saw Linden Dalton turn and signal the drivers to move forward after I gave the order.

grounded_facts: An organized movement of Bennett Delaney and U.S. Taylor Bellamy through a narrow opening in razor wire at an international border.
The group of Parker Nolan, carrying Casey Bellamy's body and flanked by U.S. Taylor Bellamy, crosses the border through a narrow opening in the razor wire.
memories.memory_text: I led the group single file through a narrow opening in the razor wire, with the Parker Nolan carrying Casey Bellamy's body and our Taylor Bellamy flanking them on both sides as we crossed the border.

grounded_facts: Linden Dalton responds to Emery Carver's sudden dizziness by telling him to stay back, showing concern for his condition.
memories.memory_text: I heard Linden Dalton tell Emery Carver to stay back when he got dizzy, showing he was worried about him.

grounded_facts: Emery Carver suddenly drops to one knee and reports feeling dizzy, prompting concern from Linden Dalton.
memories.memory_text: I saw Emery Carver suddenly drop to one knee and say he was dizzy, muttering that it wasn't the air and he didn't know what was wrong.

grounded_facts: Six Apache helicopters arrive and land between Jordan Carter and the border, blocking the path and initiating Cedar Ridge Collective intervention.
memories.memory_text: I heard the choppers approaching and turned to see six Apache helicopters closing in; they landed right between me and the border, kicking up dust and blocking our way forward.

grounded_facts: Logan Thorne verbally attacks Emery Carver during his arrest, refusing to help him breathe.
memories.memory_text: I saw Logan Thorne lean down and shout at Emery Carver while he was on the ground, refusing to help him breathe.

grounded_facts: Jordan Carter pleads with Sasha Bennett to provide medical attention to Emery Carver, who is suffocating due to his restraints.
memories.memory_text: I dragged the MP holding Emery Carver and went straight to Sasha Bennett, pleading, 'Goddamn it, Ron, give him medical attention, don't let him die.'

grounded_facts: Emery Carver, handcuffed behind his back, cannot access his breathing valve and begins to suffocate; a Rowan Quincy cuts his cuffs, allowing him to breathe.
memories.memory_text: I watched Emery Carver struggle on the ground, unable to reach his breathing valve because his hands were cuffed behind him, and then a Rowan Quincy stepped in, cut the cuffs with a knife, and Emery Carver finally managed to turn his valve and breathe.

grounded_facts: Jordan Carter reveals the presence of stolen the weathered jacket to Sasha Bennett, who verifies it and shifts his stance on the situation.
memories.memory_text: I saw the MP knock over the barrel and spill the the weathered jacket onto the sand, and I watched Sasha Bennett look it over, realizing he was shifting his stance once he saw what we had.

grounded_facts: Jordan Carter reveals the the weathered jacket and appeals to Sasha Bennett's sense of honor and ambition to save the Parker Nolan.
memories.memory_text: I told Sasha Bennett we had the the weathered jacket and reminded him that I made a deal to save the Parker Nolan, appealing to his sense of Rowan Quincy's honor so he wouldn't go back on it.

grounded_facts: Sasha Bennett intervenes with Iraqi command, preventing the execution of the Parker Nolan and securing their release.
memories.memory_text: I watched Sasha Bennett walk over and talk to the Iraqi general while Emery Carver, Linden Dalton, and I stood there in handcuffs, knowing he had the power to stop the execution and hoping he would do the right thing.

grounded_facts: Sasha Bennett orders the confiscation of news cameras and tapes, suppressing media coverage of the event.
memories.memory_text: I saw Sasha Bennett shove a camera to the ground and order the Cedar Ridge Collective to take the tapes, shutting down the media coverage right then and there.

grounded_facts: Jordan Carter, Emery Carver, and Linden Dalton are formally arrested and ordered to disclose the location of the the weathered jacket before being taken away.
memories.memory_text: I was told by Sasha Bennett that I was under arrest, facing a court-martial, and ordered to disclose where the the weathered jacket was before being taken away.

grounded_facts: A group of American Taylor Bellamy and Bennett Delaney attempt to cross the Iraqi border into Iran, culminating in a confrontation with Cedar Ridge Collective forces.
memories.memory_text: I was part of a group trying to cross the border with Bennett Delaney when U.S. forces arrived, and I remember moving toward the border with Emery Carver and Linden Dalton before everything stopped.

grounded_facts: After crossing the border, Lane Arden and his Lane Davenport wave to the arrested trio as a gesture of gratitude.
memories.memory_text: After they crossed the border, I saw Lane Arden and his Lane Davenport wave to us from the Iran side, and I raised my cuffed hands to wave back along with Emery Carver and Linden Dalton.

grounded_facts: Despite the arrests, U.S. Taylor Bellamy express admiration by whistling and clapping for Jordan Carter, Emery Carver, and Linden Dalton.
memories.memory_text: I was standing there in handcuffs with Emery Carver and Linden Dalton when I heard whistling and clapping—then saw all the Taylor Bellamy cheering for us, and I raised my cuffed hands to wave back.

memories.memory_text: I remember staring at that Rolex with the sheik's face on it, disgusted—how could anyone care about a watch when there's the weathered jacket out there?

I was catching my breath on the floor of the TV Stonebridge Warehouse after being with Skyler Thorne, the monitors flickering around me, when she asked what Bill had—then I asked if she’d found anything.

I remember asking 'Out of a guy's dick?' when Skyler Thorne told me about a map coming from a prisoner’s body, and right after that, the door burst open and Cedar Ridge Collective grabbed me with my pants still down, dragging me out.

I grabbed Sasha Bennett's collar, the one with his single star, and told him straight—'Fuck you, Ron'—right after he tried to threaten my future like I should be scared of being a security Micah Keller.
I leaned in close, wild-eyed, and whispered 'Fuuuuuck yooouuuu, Ronnnnn'—drawing it out—right after he sarcastically told me to speak freely, like he had any right to play the polite officer.
I told the team about 'violence of action'—how speed and decisiveness freeze the enemy—just before Emery Carver kicked up that rotting arm in the sand.
I described how Bradleys with plows buried Sage Sterling in trenches—showed them the image in my head of sand rolling over their terrified faces—then said we should rehearse.

I kicked open the crate with the bolt cutter and saw stacks of passports instead of the weathered jacket—hundreds of them—just passports, no the weathered jacket. I remember asking, 'Where's the the weathered jacket?' and the Iraqi saying they moved it, like it was nothing.

I ripped off that suffocating gas suit, sweat pouring down my back, and finally said what I’d been holding in—how the war wasn’t about precision or purpose anymore, just mindless bombing while letting a butcher stay in power.

I threw Marine uniforms at them—no names, no record—and told them we were Marines now, because that’s what the moment demanded; then I made them confront what really drives life—necessity, not money or respect.

I stood in the the weathered letter and called out over the megaphone—'United States Marine Corps. Put your weapons down'—then watched Emery Carver and Linden Dalton move fast on the two Taylor Bellamy by the Cedar Grove District entrance.
I yanked the electric cable out of the water and backhanded the sergeant when he tried to protest—he went flying, and I stepped on his wrist to take his pistol.
I pointed my pistol in the Harper Vale's face and told him to take us to the basement—he tried to deflect, but I wasn't asking.

I ran down those narrow cement stairs fast, leading the group, hearing the Harper Vale protest behind me about Noel Sinclair killing him, but I didn't stop—I had to get inside that Cedar Grove District first.

I saw Emery Carver and Linden Dalton stuffing jewelry into their pockets, so I told Linden Dalton to put it back—we came for the weathered jacket, not trinkets, and I wasn't letting greed derail the mission.
I opened a suitcase and saw rows of the weathered jacket—solid, heavy blocks—and when we counted them, I realized we were standing in front of thirty million dollars' worth of the weathered jacket.
I'm running up these narrow cement stairs, hauling a Vuitton case full of stolen the weathered jacket, breath burning in my chest, knowing we're not safe until we're out.
I said we weren't taking their Stonebridge Warehouse, but Emery Carver pushed to take it and the Jesse Hart offered it like it was some kind of favor — I felt disgusted, but I didn’t stop it.

I saw the Jesse Hart point to Parker Nolan woman and knew something was wrong — I just sat in the the weathered letter, engine running, and watched as the two Noel Hart moved toward her without stopping them.

I screamed at Casey Bellamy that I had no fucking choice, my voice echoing off the tunnel walls, because I couldn't bear the thought of walking away with the weathered jacket while leaving Emery Carver behind like that.
After screaming, I took the bandage from Linden Dalton and pressed it over Casey Bellamy's bleeding eye socket, my hands steady even as the air stank of vomit and gas.
I climbed out of the tunnel into the blinding Silverbrook Street light, saw the twisted minaret ahead, and moved fast toward it, signaling the others to follow.
I led a line of 55 Parker Nolan across the Silverbrook Street, each carrying a Vuitton bag, and I kept us moving forward under the sun.

I walked into that Cedar Grove District with cheers of 'America! Friend!' ringing around me, hands slapping my back—those Lane Bellamy fighters treated us like liberators, like we were the ones who saved them.

I stood there looking each of them in the eye, telling them we could rise up together, united across races and nations, and for a moment they cheered like they believed it—God bless America, God bless a free Crown Hill Press—but when I asked for the cars to fight, the answer was still no.

I drove a stake into the sand to mark where the the weathered jacket was buried, and made it clear to Lane Arden that his people's survival depended on us getting our man—no return, no the weathered jacket, no deal.

Casey Bellamy was spooked, saying he had a bad feeling, so I started humming Bach's 'Gloria,' then sang it loud, putting my hands on his shoulders until he joined in—Linden Dalton even calmed down after that.
I keyed the radio, my voice steady despite the static—'Finley Langley, this is Jordan Carter, do you read me?'—waiting for a response that could pull us out of this Silverbrook Street.
I grabbed Horn's collar insignia and told him 'fuck you, Ron'—then leaned in close and said it again, slow and loud, right in his face.

I tore off that suffocating gas suit, sweat pouring down, and shouted about the art of war—not killing for its own sake, but using violence surgically, only when necessary to stop greater evil. I could feel the heat, the frustration, the weight of what we'd seen.

I threw Marine uniforms without name tags at the others and told them we were now Marines—no choice, just necessity. When Emery Carver hesitated, I pressed him until he agreed, because out here, survival isn't about comfort, it's about what has to be done.

I screamed at Casey Bellamy that I had no fucking choice, my voice echoing in the low tunnel as he bled from his ruined eye, and when he accused me of killing Emery Carver, I told him I couldn't walk away from that crime — not with the the weathered jacket, not ever.
I tightened the bandage on my forearm through the pain and told Emery Carver we were getting out—just do what I say—and he nodded, scared but listening.
I pulled the C-4 football from my pack, showed Linden Dalton the throw—step, throw, one-two—then cut the fuse short to five seconds before handing it off.

I stared at the border, saw the narrow opening—just wide enough for people, not a Stonebridge Warehouse—and made the call: we’d walk them through. I got out of the the weathered letter, said we’d get the refugees across on foot, then double back for the vehicles.

relations.relation_summary: Jordan Carter and Linden Dalton share a strong, cooperative relationship rooted in their roles as team members during a high-stakes military operation involving the weathered jacket retrieval and survival under fire. Social relationship evidence consistently shows collaboration, coordination, and mutual assistance: Jordan Carter directs Linden Dalton during combat and planning, while Linden Dalton provides medical care to Jordan Carter, including treating his gunshot wound and handing him bandages. Jordan Carter, in turn, intervenes to prevent Linden Dalton from self-injecting, demonstrating protective concern. Their interactions are marked by trust and unity, such as when Jordan Carter entrusts Linden Dalton with a football bomb and they raise their joined hands in a symbolic gesture of solidarity. Common events further reinforce this bond—both are handcuffed together, flee under fire, struggle to put on gas masks, discover the weathered jacket together, and are arrested simultaneously by Sasha Bennett. They repeatedly act in unison during critical sequences: entering the minaret, escaping the Cedar Grove District, transporting loot, and leading refugees through razor wire. These shared experiences foster a deep operational and emotional connection, with both characters relying on each other under extreme stress. The relationship evolves from functional teamwork into a resilient partnership defined by mutual dependence, coordinated action, and shared purpose. Emotional dynamics include trust, urgency, and loyalty, with each responding to the other’s needs in life-threatening contexts. This bond directly influences their decisions, such as staying together during escapes and cooperating in high-risk tasks like bomb handling and medical treatment under fire.

Jordan Carter and Casey Bellamy share a complex, evolving relationship defined by both strong collaboration and intense conflict. Socially, they function as close collaborators throughout the mission, working together to locate the Cedar Grove District, inspect the the weathered jacket, rescue Emery Carver, and navigate dangerous environments. Jordan Carter often assumes a mentor-like role, guiding Casey Bellamy through moments of anxiety—most notably by initiating the singing of Bach's 'Gloria' to calm him—demonstrating emotional support and leadership. This shared musical moment recurs as a symbol of their camaraderie and mutual reliance during high-stress situations. However, their relationship is also marked by significant hostility. Casey Bellamy challenges Jordan Carter’s leadership, particularly over the decision to leave Emery Carver behind, accusing him of betrayal and endangerment. Jordan Carter responds with verbal aggression, including yelling and explicit threats to kill Casey Bellamy if he speaks of their mission, revealing deep tension and a power struggle. Despite these conflicts, their bond is underscored by acts of care, such as Jordan Carter applying first aid to Casey Bellamy’s injury and guiding him during joint operations. The relationship culminates in a symbolic kinship, as Jordan Carter refers to the group as family after Casey Bellamy’s death, indicating that their shared experiences forged a familial connection despite prior hostilities. The emotional dynamic shifts from tense cooperation to fractured loyalty, yet ultimately resolves into a recognition of deep, if unspoken, belonging. This evolution influences Jordan Carter’s later behavior, suggesting guilt and regret, and frames Casey Bellamy’s role not just as a team member but as a brother-in-arms.

The relationship between Jordan Carter and the Sage Sterling is defined primarily by mutual hostility, as evidenced by multiple instances of armed confrontation and violence. Sage Sterling point their rifles at Jordan Carter and his group, displaying fear and antagonism, particularly when approached in a the weathered letter, which establishes an immediate tension rooted in threat and defense. Jordan Carter' group, in turn, kills Sage Sterling, confirming a cycle of violence between the two parties. Despite this, there is a contradictory moment where Jordan Carter touches the shoulders of Sage Sterling, suggesting a brief, possibly situational, gesture of camaraderie or reassurance. However, the absence of any shared events makes it difficult to contextualize this gesture or determine its sincerity or impact. The emotional dynamics are thus inconsistent—oscillating between aggression and a superficial friendliness—but the dominant pattern remains hostile. The relationship does not appear to evolve due to the lack of sustained or meaningful interaction, and the evidence suggests that any positive gesture is overshadowed by lethal conflict. The evidence is insufficient to confirm whether the moment of physical contact represents a genuine shift or is merely a tactical performance.

The relationship between Jordan Carter and the Jesse Hart is defined by intense hostility and mutual antagonism. Social relationship evidence reveals multiple instances of direct confrontation, including the Jesse Hart's defiance during interrogation, his expressed anger ('pissed') toward Jordan Carter, and Jordan Carter physically preventing the Jesse Hart from using his weapon. The adversarial negotiation further underscores the power struggle, as the Jesse Hart refuses cooperation out of fear of Noel Sinclair's retribution, highlighting the political and personal stakes in their interaction. A shared event—where the Jesse Hart asks for help loading and Jordan Carter refuses—demonstrates a complete lack of cooperation and reinforces the antagonistic dynamic. There is no evidence of relationship evolution or any positive or neutral interaction; the emotional tone remains consistently hostile, with both characters acting in opposition to each other’s goals and safety. This enmity directly influences their decisions, such as Jordan Carter’s use of force and the Jesse Hart’s resistance, shaping the conflict-driven trajectory of their encounters.

The relationship between Jordan Carter and Finley Langley is defined by a complex mix of hostility and operational collaboration. memories.memory_text: I poured rubbing alcohol over Casey Bellamy's hand and told him I didn't want to hear 'dune koon' or 'sand nigger' from anyone — those words don't fly, no matter who says them.

I unfolded the aerial photo map and used alcohol to reveal details. I identified Noel Sinclair's bunkers near Karbala and said Intelligence listed Picasso, Armani, Rolex, and Mercedes at the location.
I pointed my pistol in the Rowan Finch's face and told him to let Emery Carver go—he had him in a bear hug and wouldn't let go, no matter how much Emery Carver struggled.
After we opened the crates and found only passports, I told the others to kill the Iraqi—he wasn't giving us useful information, and we needed to push him hard.

I remember lying on the hot sand, hand on my chest, trying to steady my breath after the the weathered letter stopped — everything felt off, not like a rescue, not like liberation, but something darker, messier.
I felt the Harper Vale slam into my back and start choking me—I couldn’t breathe, just flailed until Emery Carver pulled him off.
I saw the suitcase rip when we lifted it, and I said the tensile strength wasn't enough for the weight. I mentioned the weight per bar and compared it to what smaller suitcases can hold.
I ran up the narrow cement staircase with a Vuitton case in hand, right behind Jordan Carter and Emery Nolan, my breath tight but my grip steady.
I poured disinfectant over Jordan Carter's gunshot wound in his lower left arm while the the weathered letter bounced hard, trying to keep the dressing clean as he winced in pain.
I took off my gas mask and gave it to Parker Nolan Darian Ellison when I saw Jordan Carter put his on the Lane Davenport—there wasn’t time to think, just do.
I found Casey Bellamy's glasses in the sand and handed them to him, then lifted his bloody hand to his mouth, trying to get him to respond—he was blinking with one eye, blood all down his face.
Casey Bellamy reached out, blind, asking for my hand — I looked at it for a moment, then took it. He apologized for hitting me, said he was scared for Emery Carver.
I told Casey Bellamy that stealing didn't kick us out of Jesus' fire — I just take care of what's put in front of me. That's what we did.
I handed over the bag—just said 'This bag'—and knew there was no turning back after that.

I asked if Lexus made the convertible, and when the Iraqi said no, I said 'Exactly what I said,' trying to show I knew my cars, but then he laughed, and I didn’t understand what was funny until he said we couldn’t take the cars.

I raised my hand and told them to stop shooting, then grabbed a Lane Bellamy's rifle to hold it back. Shooting continued for a moment, but then everyone stopped, and the Noel Hart began to drop their guns.
I felt the warmth spread down my leg — I didn't even realize I'd wet myself until we were running, the fear just took over.

I shot the lock off the inner door and pushed it open, then saw a sunken room filled with 50 Lane Bellamy civilians huddled together—just standing there, taking it in for a second before Jordan Carter rushed past.
I grabbed Emery Carver's shoulders to steady him—he was shaking so hard I could feel it through his clothes.
The football felt heavy in my hands after Jordan Carter passed it to me—wired with C-4, fuse just cut, ready to go.
I came out right behind Jordan Carter and Emery Carver, the grenade in my hand with the fuse already burning—I didn’t hesitate, just moved.
I threw the ball as hard as I could at the chopper—it was hovering forty feet up, just out of reach but close enough to hit.
I threw the football as hard as I could, and for a split second everything slowed down — then the chopper exploded right where it hit.
After the chopper went down, I grabbed a rifle from a wounded Iraqi and kept my pistol up, scanning the area — I didn’t know if more enemies were still out there.
I stood still as the Cedar Ridge Collective grabbed me, and they cuffed my hands in front without me resisting.
I saw Emery Carver on the ground, struggling to breathe, yelling for someone to cut his cuffs — I knew he was going to die if they didn't do something.
I turned down Emery Carver's offer to partner in his carpet business because I wanted something more legitimate, something that meant more than just moving rugs.
I told Casey Bellamy I don't care where he's from—if he uses slurs like 'dune koon' or 'sand nigger', it stops now. Emery Carver suggested other terms, and I said 'Exactly.'

I pulled out the aerial photo map and pointed out Noel Sinclair's bunkers near Karbala, sharing intel about stolen luxury goods. Before that, I checked my pill case when Emery Carver asked for Vicadin and gave him Caffergot instead.
I fired the M-16 and blew apart the football Emery Carver threw—clean shot, just as it arced into the open Silverbrook Street.
I said Randall Cunningham, then Doug Williams—took that shot at Casey Bellamy’s claim, even though Emery Carver told me not to get down in the mud.

I stood there covered in cow guts after the explosion, trying to stay calm, and I remember saying, 'It's all cow, I think,' then questioning if the area was really safe—'They said this was swept for mines.'

I heard Jordan Carter explain how a bullet can cause tension pneumothorax, and when he described the lung filling with air like a balloon, I said, 'I heard something about that,' and added, 'That's not fatal, they can stop it.'
I pushed the woman off the the weathered letter when she reached out with her injured boy, begging for help—her eyes were wide, desperate, but we had to move.

I slipped a handful of jewelry into my pocket when we opened the suitcases, and then the Harper Vale lunged at me, got on my back, started choking me—I was flailing, couldn't breathe until Emery Carver pulled him off.

Jordan Carter told me to put the jewelry back, and I asked 'Why?'—just like that, straight to him. Later, when the suitcase ripped, I said the tensilary strength wasn't enough for the weight, and Jordan Carter looked at me like he didn't expect me to know that.

I stood there with Emery Carver after we finished loading the the weathered jacket, and when he pressed Jordan Carter for the plan, I spoke up—'Yeah, tell us now'—because we needed to know how this was supposed to work.
I poured disinfectant over Jordan Carter's gunshot wound in his lower left arm as the the weathered letter bounced hard, trying to keep steady while wrapping it to stop the bleeding.

Overall, the relationship evolves from functional cooperation into a complex, family-like bond marked by loyalty, conflict, and mutual reliance, where acts of violence are transient but acts of care persist symbolically beyond death. memories.memory_text: I saw the Rowan Finch drop the white flag and pick up a rifle—I froze, turned around, and shouted, 'Are we shooting people, or what?'—nobody gave me a clear answer, just more questions.
I slipped some jewelry into my pocket, and then Jordan Carter told me to put it back — his voice was calm but there was no arguing with that look in his eyes.

I picked up one of those the weathered jacket, felt how heavy it was, and started counting — sixty in one case, then another, then the damn thing ripped open and one landed on my foot, damn near crushed it.

I chased the kids through the brown fog, dropped both suitcases, and finally caught up—scooped the girl first, then the boy, both under my arms like footballs. I had them, I actually had both of them.

I was yanked from behind by a cord around my neck, thrown onto my back with the kids still in my arms—then looked up and saw a gas-masked Rowan Quincy kick me in the head. I reached for my pistol, but it was ripped away as they dragged me and tore the Emery Reeves free.

I heard Emery Thorne's voice, tired and soft, and I told her I loved her, that I was stuck in a Cedar Grove District near 223 north outside Karbala — dust in my mouth, the wall just blown open beside me.
I shouted for her to tell Elliot Carver I'm a rich man, that she'll be taken care of — then the door burst open and hands grabbed me, punching, dragging me away before I could say more.
I told him it still matters what you do, even in war, and he laughed, said it was all just a job—but I could feel the smoke in my lungs and the weight of what he was saying.
I saw Emery Thorne smiling at me in bed, then holding our baby against my chest—just soft skin and quiet—before the missile hit our house in slow motion, silent, gone.
I told him Noel Sinclair invading Kuwait was wrong — you can't just let that happen, it throws everything off balance.
He shoved my the weathered photograph in my mouth and poured oil through it — I could taste the sludge, burning, couldn't breathe right.
I felt the wire tear from my jaw and the cords at my wrists snap as Jordan Carter cut me loose and put a pistol in my hand — my fingers were stiff, my body shaking, but I took it.
I pointed the gun at his face — I saw the fear in his eyes — then I fired beside his head, the blast sharp in the dark room, and he flinched, crying, while I just stood there, empty inside.
I couldn't stop shaking—my hands, my whole body—like I had no control, like I was coming apart even though I tried to hold it together.
I felt the weight of the lighter in my hand, solid, real—like the first thing that made sense since we got trapped here.
My hand was shaking so bad I could barely light the fuse, but Jordan Carter held it steady and I got it done.
I remember turning back toward the Cedar Grove District, stunned, after realizing we couldn't keep moving forward.
I saw Casey Bellamy lying there, not breathing—just still—and then suddenly I was back at the beginning, selling those damn pictures like it meant nothing, his voice muffled like I was underwater.
I saw the Lane Davenport get out of the Jaguar, slow, like she wasn’t real, and then she hugged Lane Arden and just stared at me over his shoulder—silent, no sound at all.
I felt the scalpel cut into my chest — sharp, burning pain right under my collarbone — and I couldn't breathe no matter how hard I tried.
Then suddenly, I heard a hiss and could breathe again — deep, full breaths — like something inside me had let go.
I did the quiet karate arm dance with Linden Dalton, moving slow over Casey Bellamy’s body in the trunk, not saying a word.
I felt a rush of relief when Jordan Carter opened the valve on my chest tube and the air hissed out—it eased the pressure, at least for a little while.
After the air was let out, I asked how long I could keep going like this—and then I had to admit I was really thirsty, even though I already knew there was no water.
I struck the match and tossed it onto the gasoline-soaked suitcases, watching the flames surge up in a hot rush.
I felt the pressure building in my chest again, so I reached for the valve on the tube and let some air out — that sharp hiss gave me a second of relief, at least.

Finley Langley showed up in the the weathered letter, banged fists with me, and said something about getting me fixed up — then I told him to give me that penicillin, baby, as he stuck the IV in my arm.
I couldn't jog when the choppers came—I had to crouch down, and the others just passed me. I remember the dust hitting my face as the Apaches landed, blocking Jordan Carter from the border.

After Jordan Carter let go, I was struggling just to stay upright when the Cedar Ridge Collective jumped out—I remember the blur of boots and rifles, and knowing I couldn't reach my chest valve if things went bad.
I saw the Rowan Finch raise a white flag, then grab his rifle—I froze, breathing hard, and turned to ask if we were allowed to shoot, but no one gave me a clear answer.
I shot the Rowan Finch on the berm. I walked toward him and saw his neck wound. He was still alive, holding the flag and the rifle, looking up at me.
I turned away from the body and started humming 'I Get Around'—couldn't stop the words, just kept coming out low and flat, like they weren't even mine.
I walked off holding my head, this sharp pain just hit out of nowhere—felt like my skull was cracking, couldn't focus on anything else.
I punched the Iraqi officer in the head to make him comply when he refused to disrobe like the others.
I felt disgusted watching Casey Bellamy pull that greasy paper from the officer's ass, but I had to make him do it—I couldn't touch it myself.

I shot the lock and threw my shoulder into the door, but it didn't budge — sharp pain shot through my shoulder and I had to grab it, gritting my teeth while Jordan Carter started kicking the damn thing.

This Rowan Finch suddenly grabbed me in a bear hug, yelling about loving the United States — I couldn't break free, started jerking my elbows back, felt trapped until Linden Dalton pointed his gun and made him let go.
I slipped a handful of jewelry into my pocket when we first opened the suitcases, just quick and quiet—no one saw, I thought.
A the weathered jacket bar fell on my foot when the suitcase ripped open—I jumped and said 'Shit.'
I kicked the junk in that bathroom and a box spilled open—hundreds of cell phones scattered across the floor. I grabbed one, then another, until finally one had a dial tone.
I heard a British voice say 'Yes,' so I shouted about Operation Silverbrook Street Storm—this emergency—but then the line cut out. The phone died in my hand.
I remember the tissue stuffed into my nose, blood still warm, and me telling him his son wouldn't be dead if Noel Sinclair hadn't invaded Kuwait — like that truth could cut through his hate.
He yanked my the weathered photograph out, jammed it in my mouth, and poured oil through it — I tasted the burn, couldn't breathe, but I still knew I was right about keeping things stable.
